tickets.title: Structured JSON logging with redaction processor
tickets.summary: Every log line is JSON with the 9.3 field set and passes through a redactor that drops bodies, queries, prompts and exception text.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.3: "Structured JSON to stdout, redacted before writing: ts, severity, trace, request_id, tenant_id, advisor_hash, event, error_code. No request bodies, queries, prompts, tool payloads or exception text for clients."
Extend backend/src/observability/logging.py (structlog already present; it currently binds user_id and renders exception info). Build:
- Processors producing exactly the keys ts, severity, trace (Cloud Trace id from the current OTel span, empty if none), request_id, tenant_id, advisor_hash (sha256 of advisor_id, never the raw id), event, error_code, plus event-specific scalar fields.
- A redaction processor with a denylist of keys (body, query, prompt, message, messages, content, tool_input, tool_output, sql, params, exc_info, exception, traceback, authorization, token) that replaces the value with "[redacted]", and runs the E4 PII scrubber (backend/src/pii) over remaining string values.
- Remove format_exc_info: log error_code and exception class name only.
- bind_request_context takes request_id, tenant_id, advisor_id (hash applied inside).
Out of scope: Kong file-log (E2-T15), Langfuse masking (E0-T8), spans (E9-T2), log-based metric definitions (E9-T11).
acceptance_criteria: Given logger.info('x', body='secret text', query='SELECT 1', error_code='INTERNAL'), When captured by a test sink, Then the JSON has body and query equal to '[redacted]', contains the keys ts, severity, trace, request_id, tenant_id, advisor_hash, event, error_code, and the test fails if any other key carries the secret text (pytest backend/tests/observability/test_logging.py).

Given logger.exception inside an except ValueError('card 4111 1111 1111 1111'), When captured, Then the line has no 'traceback' or 'exc_info' key and the string '4111' does not appear anywhere in the line.
Given bound advisor_id='adv-123', When a line is logged, Then advisor_hash is a 64-hex sha256 and 'adv-123' does not appear in the line.

Given an active OTel span, When a line is logged, Then trace equals the span's trace id in Cloud Trace format projects/

/traces/; with no span it is an empty string.

tickets.title: OpenTelemetry bootstrap for chat-api and workers
tickets.summary: One shared init function configures OTel tracing with FastAPI, asyncpg and HTTP client instrumentation, SQL parameter capture off, exporting to the OTLP endpoint.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.1: "OpenTelemetry end to end: Kong opentelemetry (traceparent) to chat-api (FastAPI, asyncpg / SQLAlchemy, Voyage and Anthropic HTTP calls) to workers ... to Cloud Trace. SQL parameter capture off; no request bodies in spans (D13o)." Stack: OpenTelemetry SDK + exporters, versions pinned at implementation (stack.md).
Build backend/src/observability/tracing.py (exists; rework) with init_tracing(service_name) used by the chat-api app factory and by the worker/job entrypoints:
- TracerProvider with resource service.name, deployment.environment = ENV_PROFILE; OTLP exporter to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (config key, required); BatchSpanProcessor.
- W3C traceparent propagation; FastAPI instrumentation continues the traceparent Kong sends.
- asyncpg / SQLAlchemy instrumentation with parameter capture controlled only by OTEL_DB_CAPTURE_PARAMS (default false; the db.statement attribute is replaced by the operation and table, no literals).
- httpx/aiohttp instrumentation for Voyage and Anthropic calls with request/response body and header capture disabled.
- A SpanProcessor that deletes any attribute whose key is in the E9-T1 denylist or that is longer than 256 characters.
- init is a no-op when the endpoint is unset in dev profile.
Out of scope: span names in the turn pipeline (E9-T3), worker spans (E9-T4), the Kong plugin (E2-T15).
Export path (resolution R77): direct OTLP to the Google Cloud Telemetry API endpoint (telemetry.googleapis.com) authenticated with Application Default Credentials; no sidecar. FIRST step of this ticket is a verification: send a test span from a Cloud Run service (or a scratch project with ADC) and confirm it appears in Cloud Trace. Write the outcome to docs/adr/otel-export.md. If direct export fails, the fallback is an OTel Collector sidecar on Cloud Run; record that decision, the evidence and the changed deployment in the same ADR before building it. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: Given OTEL_DB_CAPTURE_PARAMS=false, When a query 'SELECT * FROM advisors WHERE email = $1' runs with a parameter 'a@b.com' under an in-memory exporter, Then no exported span attribute value contains 'a@b.com' (pytest test_tracing_sql.py).
Given a request with a traceparent header, When it hits GET /healthz, Then the exported server span has the same trace_id and its parent_span_id equals the header's span id.
Given an httpx call to a stubbed api.anthropic.com with a JSON body containing 'SECRETPROMPT', When exported, Then no span attribute contains 'SECRETPROMPT'.
Given an attribute named 'body' or a 300-char value is set on a span, When the span ends, Then the exported span lacks it.

Given the verification run, When a span is exported with ADC to the Telemetry API endpoint, Then it is returned by the Cloud Trace API (gcloud/REST get trace) within 60 s, and docs/adr/otel-export.md exists with the result and the fallback decision (CI file-presence check fails if the ADR is missing).

tickets.title: Instrument the chat turn with the named spans
tickets.summary: The chat turn emits chat.turn and its child spans with the 9.1 names and only non-sensitive attributes.
tickets.description:
Implements the span-name list of overview.md 9.1: chat.turn, auth.verify, principal.load, guard.input, guard.model_armor, embed.query, retrieval.hybrid_sql, retrieval.rerank, retrieval.gate, llm.stream, guard.output, persist.turn.
Add backend/src/observability/spans.py: constants for the names above and a helper span(name, **attrs) that rejects (raises in tests, drops in prod) attributes outside an allowlist (tenant_id, turn_id, model, token counts, chunk_count, degraded, gate_result, cache_hit, error_code). Wrap the existing call sites in auth, principal, guardrails, retrieval, llm, agent and persistence code in the matching span. chat.turn is the parent; llm.stream carries model, input/output/cache-read token counts; retrieval.gate carries gate_result. Spans must not carry query text, prompts, chunk text or SQL parameters.
Out of scope: changing the behaviour of those stages; Langfuse generations (E0-T8); worker spans (E9-T4).
acceptance_criteria: Given one stubbed POST /v1/chat that is answered, When spans are collected with an in-memory exporter, Then all twelve span names exist, share one trace_id, and every one except chat.turn has a parent in the trace (pytest test_turn_spans.py).
Given a refusal turn (gate refuses), When collected, Then retrieval.gate has gate_result='refused' and no llm.stream span exists.
Given span('x', query='abc'), When run under pytest, Then it raises ValueError; with ENV_PROFILE=prod it drops the attribute and the exported span lacks it.
Given the turn, When exported, Then llm.stream has integer attributes for input, output and cache-read tokens.

tickets.title: Link consumer spans to producer spans over Kafka headers
tickets.summary: outbox.relay and consumer.<role> spans are emitted and each consumer span carries a span link to the producing span from the traceparent header.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.1: "workers (traceparent carried in Kafka headers)", spans outbox.relay and consumer.<role>. The producer wrapper already sets traceparent (E5-T6) and the consumer base class exists (E5-T7).
Build: in the outbox-relay role (E5-T10) wrap each publish in an outbox.relay span, writing the current context into the Kafka traceparent header (via the E5-T6 wrapper, do not duplicate it). In the consumer base (E5-T7) start consumer.<role> for each message with a Link to the SpanContext extracted from traceparent (a link, not a parent, so batch/retry does not stretch traces); retries and DLQ publishing (E5-T8) stay inside the span. Attributes: topic, partition, offset, tenant_id, role, outcome. No payloads.
Out of scope: producer header logic, consumer semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given a message produced inside a span S through the E5-T6 wrapper and consumed by the E5-T7 base in a test with an in-memory exporter, When the handler finishes, Then a span named 'consumer.<role>' exists whose links contain S's trace_id and span_id (pytest test_consumer_links.py).
Given a message without a traceparent header, When consumed, Then consumer.<role> is still emitted with no links and no exception.
Given a handler that raises, When retried then sent to the DLQ, Then the span has outcome='dlq' and error_code set, and its attributes contain no payload text.
Given the outbox-relay role publishes 3 rows, When collected, Then three outbox.relay spans exist, each with topic and tenant_id attributes.

tickets.title: Shared metrics module and 9.2 metric registry
tickets.summary: One module owns metric names, types and labels from the 9.2 table and records them to OTel and to a log line for log-based metrics.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.2: "Metrics (log-based and OTel, in Cloud Monitoring)". Create backend/src/observability/metrics.py:
- A registry listing every metric in the table with name, kind (counter, histogram, gauge), unit and allowed labels: chat_ttft_ms, chat_total_ms, retrieval_first_stage_ms, rerank_ms, rerank_fallback_total{reason}, rerank_429_total, retrieval_degraded_ratio, gate_refusals_total, guard_blocks_total{guard}, llm_fallback_total, llm_breaker_state, answer_cache_hit_ratio, outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag{group}, acl_apply_lag_s, dlq_messages_total, tenant_budget_rejections_total{tenant}, default_partition_rows, db_connections_in_use.
- record(name, value, **labels) that rejects unknown names or labels and records through the OTel metrics API (OTLP) and also writes one structured log line (event='metric', metric, value, labels) through the E9-T1 logger so log-based metrics work.
- Existing emitters from E3-T9, E4 and E5 are migrated to call record() where they currently do something else; do not change their values.
Out of scope: dashboards, alerts, new emitters (E9-T6, E9-T7).
Add to the registry (resolutions R73, R74): llm_cost_usd_total{provider,model} (counter, USD), readiness_failing (gauge 0/1) and model_retirement_days (gauge, days until the earliest retirement of a configured model). The registry now has 22 metrics; the 9.2 table copy in backend/tests/observability/metrics_9_2.txt includes these three (the architecture table §9.2 gains these rows). Earlier epics emit with plain OTel meters; this ticket moves them to the registry (R71).
acceptance_criteria: Given record('not_a_metric', 1), When called, Then it raises KeyError; given record('rerank_fallback_total', 1, reason='x', extra='y'), Then it raises on the unknown label (pytest test_metrics_registry.py).

Given the registry, When compared with the metric names parsed from the overview.md 9.2 table copied into backend/tests/observability/metrics_9_2.txt, Then the sets are equal (the test fails if one is added or missing).
Given record('chat_ttft_ms', 1200), When captured, Then one OTel data point and one log line with event='metric', metric='chat_ttft_ms' and value 1200 exist.
Given a label value tenant_id longer than 64 chars or containing newline, When recorded, Then it is rejected or truncated so the log line stays a single JSON line.

Given record('llm_cost_usd_total', 0.01, provider='anthropic', model='x'), When captured, Then it is accepted; with a label other than provider and model it raises; the registry has exactly the 22 names in metrics_9_2.txt.

tickets.title: Emit chat latency, cache, budget, DB pool and LLM cost metrics
tickets.summary: The chat path emits the 9.2 metrics no other epic owns: TTFT, total latency, cache ratio, tenant budget rejections and connection use.
tickets.description:
Implements the 9.2 rows for chat_ttft_ms, chat_total_ms, answer_cache_hit_ratio, tenant_budget_rejections_total{tenant} and db_connections_in_use. Retrieval metrics are emitted by E3-T9, guard and LLM metrics (guard_blocks_total, llm_fallback_total, llm_breaker_state, gate_refusals_total) by E4, acl_apply_lag_s by E5; do not touch those.
Using metrics.record (E9-T5): in the chat orchestrator record chat_ttft_ms at the first delta event and chat_total_ms at done (also on errors, with the elapsed time); record answer_cache_hit_ratio as a rolling ratio gauge over the last N turns (window config constant, default 100); record tenant_budget_rejections_total when TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED is returned; sample db_connections_in_use from the asyncpg pool every 15 s in a background task (pool size is DB_POOL_SIZE; budget is 300 connections overall, 9.2).
If E4 already emits any of these names, keep one emitter and delete the duplicate (check with grep before coding).
Also emit llm_cost_usd_total{provider,model} (R73): cost = input/output/cache-read/cache-write token counts from each Anthropic call (and Voyage embed/rerank usage) multiplied by a price table in config (new Settings key LLM_PRICE_TABLE_JSON, a mapping provider/model to USD per million tokens by token kind; a missing model logs a warning and records 0 with a label-free counter llm_cost_unpriced). Recorded in the llm client after each call; no payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stubbed turn with the first delta after 1.2 s and done after 3.0 s using a fake clock, When it completes, Then chat_ttft_ms=1200 and chat_total_ms=3000 are recorded exactly once each (pytest test_chat_metrics.py).
Given 3 cache hits and 1 miss, When answer_cache_hit_ratio is read, Then it is 0.75.
Given a tenant over its budget, When POST /v1/chat is called, Then the response error code is TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED and tenant_budget_rejections_total{tenant} increments by 1.
Given a pool with 4 connections acquired, When the sampler runs, Then db_connections_in_use=4. A grep test asserts each of these five names is recorded in exactly one module.

Given a stubbed call with 1000 input and 500 output tokens on a model priced at $3 and $15 per million, When completed, Then llm_cost_usd_total{provider='anthropic',model=<m>} increases by 0.0105 (pytest test_llm_cost.py).
Given a model absent from LLM_PRICE_TABLE_JSON, When called, Then no exception is raised and llm_cost_unpriced increments by 1.

tickets.title: Emit event-pipeline and partition health metrics
tickets.summary: outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag, dlq_messages_total and default_partition_rows are emitted on a schedule.
tickets.description:
Implements the 9.2 rows for outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag{group}, dlq_messages_total and default_partition_rows ("rows in the DEFAULT chunks / messages partitions (bug signal)"). acl_apply_lag_s is E5's.
Using metrics.record (E9-T5):
- Worker background task (every 30 s, in roles outbox-relay and the consumer roles): outbox_oldest_age_s = now - min(created_at) of unpublished outbox rows (0 if none), read through the worker's tenant-safe path; consumer_lag{group} = end offset minus committed offset summed over the group's partitions; dlq_messages_total incremented in the E5-T8 DLQ publisher.
- default_partition_rows: count rows in chunks_default and messages_default (names as created by E1 migrations; check the schema) recorded as a gauge, emitted from the maintenance job (E1-T12) after its checks, with the job still exiting non-zero as E1-T12 defines.
Out of scope: alerting (E9-T15), the maintenance job's exit code.
The maintenance job runs every 15 min in demo mode (E10 schedules it, R76), so default_partition_rows is refreshed at that cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unpublished outbox row created 90 s ago in a test DB, When the sampler runs, Then outbox_oldest_age_s is between 90 and 95; with no unpublished rows it is 0 (pytest test_pipeline_metrics.py, integration with Postgres).
Given a consumer group committed at offset 10 with end offset 25 on one partition in the local Kafka, When sampled, Then consumer_lag{group}=15.
Given a message that exhausts retries, When published to dlq.v1, Then dlq_messages_total increments by 1.
Given one row inserted into the DEFAULT messages partition, When the maintenance job runs, Then default_partition_rows=1 is recorded and the job exits non-zero; with none it records 0 and exits zero.

tickets.title: Complete /readyz with the 9.4 checks
tickets.summary: /readyz asserts every item in the 9.4 list and returns a per-check result, with Kafka failing only as degraded.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 6.1 and 9.4: "/readyz (DB role flags, FORCE RLS, partition grants, pgvector >= 0.8, Kafka reachability (degraded for chat), model availability, verifier initialised)". E0-T5 built /healthz and /readyz with database and model checks; E4-T7 added the retired-model check. Extend, do not rewrite:
- Checks: db_reachable, role_flags (fa_app and fa_worker lack BYPASSRLS and SUPERUSER), force_rls (every tenant table has relforcerowsecurity), partition_grants (the app roles hold privileges on the current and future partitions of chunks and messages), pgvector_version >= 0.8, kafka_reachable (metadata request with a 2 s timeout), models_available (reuse the retired-model check), verifier_initialised (firebase-admin app created).
- Response 200 {status: 'ok' or 'degraded', checks: {name: 'ok'|'fail'|'degraded'}}; Kafka failure gives status 'degraded' and HTTP 200; any other failure gives 503. No error text, hostnames or credentials in the body.
- Record readiness_failing (gauge 0/1) via metrics.record for alerting (add it to the registry and to the 9.2 test list as an addition recorded in questions if not accepted).
Out of scope: /healthz, Kong's status listener, the demo-prewarm call.
readiness_failing (gauge 0/1) is part of the 9.2 registry (R74); it is set from the same checks as /readyz on each probe and by a 15 s background task. model_retirement_days is set by the E0-T4 check at each probe.
acceptance_criteria: Given a test DB where fa_app has BYPASSRLS, When GET /readyz, Then status 503 and checks.role_flags='fail' (pytest test_readyz.py).
Given a table with FORCE RLS disabled, Then 503 with force_rls='fail'; given pgvector 0.7, Then 503 with pgvector_version='fail'.
Given the Kafka broker unreachable and everything else healthy, When GET /readyz, Then HTTP 200 with status='degraded' and kafka_reachable='degraded'.
Given any failure, When the response body is serialised, Then it contains none of the DB host, user or exception text (assert on string).
Given a failing check, When /readyz is probed, Then readiness_failing=1; after recovery it is 0 (pytest).

tickets.title: Leak test for logs, spans and metrics
tickets.summary: A test fails if any log line, span, metric label or trace contains a request body, SQL parameter or unredacted PII after a full turn.
tickets.description:
Implements the Done-when item: "no log line, span or trace contains request bodies, SQL parameters or unredacted PII (test)". E4-T25 already tests that PII does not reach Voyage, Anthropic, logs or Langfuse; this ticket covers the E9 additions (spans, metric labels, consumer spans) and keeps one canary approach: do not repeat E4-T25's cases, reuse its canary fixtures.
Add backend/tests/observability/test_no_leaks.py (integration, local compose with Postgres and Kafka): run a chat turn with canary message text 'CANARY-BODY-7731 jane.doe@example.com 123-45-6789', an ACL change and an eval-sampled event; capture stdout log lines, all spans from an in-memory exporter (including attributes, events and links), and all metric data points and labels; assert none contains the canary strings or the SQL parameter values bound in that run.
Out of scope: Langfuse payloads (E0-T8, E4-T25).
acceptance_criteria: Given the canary turn, When all logs, spans and metric labels are searched, Then zero matches for 'CANARY-BODY-7731', 'jane.doe@example.com' and '123-45-6789' (pytest test_no_leaks.py fails otherwise).
Given OTEL_DB_CAPTURE_PARAMS=true is set by the test, When the same run happens, Then the test fails, proving it can detect parameter capture.
Given a deliberately injected logger.info(body=canary) via a test-only hook, When the redactor is bypassed, Then the test fails (negative control).
Given the full suite in CI, When it runs, Then this test is included in the required checks.

tickets.title: End-to-end trace test across Kong, API, DB and LLM
tickets.summary: A compose test proves one trace spans Kong, chat-api, a DB query and an LLM call, and a Kafka consumer links to its producer.
tickets.description:
Implements the Done-when item: "A single trace spans Kong, chat-api, a DB query and an LLM call, and a Kafka event's consumer span links to its producer span."
Add an integration test run against docker compose with Kong (opentelemetry plugin from E2-T15), chat-api, Postgres, Kafka, a worker, an OpenTelemetry Collector with a file or debug exporter writing spans as JSON, and a stubbed Anthropic/Voyage endpoint. The test sends POST /v1/chat, then reads collector output and asserts the span tree. Add the collector service and config to the compose file and set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for services. Document how to run it in docs/runbooks/observability.md.
Out of scope: Cloud Trace itself (verified manually in the E9-T17 drill note).
acceptance_criteria: Given the compose stack up, When POST /v1/chat is sent through Kong, Then collector output holds one trace_id containing a Kong span, chat.turn, a DB span (asyncpg) and llm.stream with a child HTTP client span (pytest -m e2e test_e2e_trace.py).
Given a turn that writes an outbox row, When the relay publishes and the worker consumes, Then a consumer.<role> span exists whose link's trace_id equals the turn's trace_id.
Given the Kong plugin disabled, When the test runs, Then it fails on the missing Kong span (negative check documented in the test).
Given the e2e run, When the span dump is scanned, Then no span attribute contains the request message text.

tickets.title: Terraform: log-based metrics and notification channel
tickets.summary: Terraform defines the log-based metrics and the alert notification channel used by all dashboards and alert policies.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.2 "log-based and OTel, in Cloud Monitoring" for metrics emitted as log lines (event='metric', E9-T5), and creates the notification channel the alerts in 9.5 use. Existing terraform/ has main.tf, cloud_run.tf, variables.tf; add terraform/monitoring.tf.
- google_logging_metric (distribution or counter, label extractors on metric and labels) for every 9.2 metric that is emitted by log line; metrics emitted over OTLP need no resource here.
- google_monitoring_notification_channel (email) with the address from a variable alert_email (required).
- Variables env_profile (matches ENV_PROFILE) used by later tickets.
Out of scope: dashboards (E9-T12), SLOs (E9-T13), alert policies (E9-T14, E9-T15).
Notification channel: email to alert_email (R75).
acceptance_criteria: Given terraform validate and terraform plan -var-file=ci.tfvars, When run in CI, Then both succeed with no errors.

Given the plan output, When listed, Then one google_logging_metric exists for each name in the E9-T5 registry that is log-emitted and the notification channel exists (a script scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py compares names to the registry and fails on a gap).
Given a log line event='metric', metric='rerank_ms', value=412, When tested against the metric's filter with gcloud logging read in the drill (E9-T17), Then it matches and the extractor yields 412.
Given alert_email unset, When terraform plan, Then it errors (required variable).

tickets.title: Terraform: four Cloud Monitoring dashboards
tickets.summary: Dashboards chat, retrieval, events and cost exist as code and together show every 9.2 metric.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.5: "Dashboards in Cloud Monitoring (one per concern: chat, retrieval, events, cost)". Add terraform/dashboards/*.json and google_monitoring_dashboard resources in terraform/dashboards.tf.
- chat: chat_ttft_ms and chat_total_ms p50/p95 with the SLO lines (3.5 s, 2.0 s, 8 s), gate_refusals_total, guard_blocks_total by guard, llm_fallback_total, llm_breaker_state, answer_cache_hit_ratio, error rate.
- retrieval: retrieval_first_stage_ms and rerank_ms p95 with lines 300 and 700 ms, rerank_fallback_total by reason, rerank_429_total, retrieval_degraded_ratio.
- events: outbox_oldest_age_s, consumer_lag by group, acl_apply_lag_s, dlq_messages_total, default_partition_rows.
- cost: db_connections_in_use against 300, tenant_budget_rejections_total by tenant, Kong prometheus series, billing spend widget.
Each dashboard's metric names come from the registry; Kong prometheus series appear only where exported.
acceptance_criteria: Given the E9-T5 registry, When scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py runs, Then every one of its 19 names appears in at least one dashboard JSON; the check fails if one is missing.
Given terraform validate, When run in CI, Then it passes; given terraform apply to a scratch project in the drill, Then four dashboards are listed by gcloud monitoring dashboards list.
Given the chat dashboard JSON, When parsed, Then threshold lines of 3500, 2000 and 8000 ms exist on the right charts (jq assertions in the check script).
Given the retrieval dashboard JSON, Then threshold lines at 300 and 700 ms exist.

tickets.title: Terraform: availability and latency SLOs with burn-rate alerts
tickets.summary: SLOs for availability (prod only), latency and retrieval exist with multi-window burn-rate alerts whose thresholds are fixed in the ticket.
tickets.description:
Implements overview.md 9.5 SLO table: availability 99.5% monthly of chat requests not failing, prod profile only; TTFT p95 < 3.5 s (p50 < 2.0 s) and full answer p95 < 8 s on demo and prod; retrieval first stage p95 < 300 ms, rerank p95 < 700 ms on both. "Windows and thresholds set in E9."
Add google_monitoring_slo resources in terraform/slo.tf over a custom service for chat-api. Availability SLO created only when env_profile == "prod" (count). Burn-rate alert policies: fast (1 h window with 5 min lookback, burn rate 14.4) and slow (6 h window with 30 min lookback, burn rate 6), the standard multi-window values for a 99.5% target; record the choice and the budget (0.5% of a 30-day window = about 3.6 h) in docs/runbooks/slo.md. A chat request fails when the response is HTTP 5xx or the SSE stream ends with an error event other than the intended refusals/4xx codes; define the good/total filter in the doc.
Out of scope: other alerts.
Burn-rate numbers fixed by R72: 14.4x over 1 h and 6x over 6 h.
acceptance_criteria: Given env_profile=prod, When terraform plan, Then one availability SLO with goal 0.995 and rolling 30-day period and two burn-rate alert policies are planned; given env_profile=demo, Then the availability SLO and its alerts are absent and the latency SLOs remain (CI plan assertions through terraform show -json).
Given the plan JSON, When checked, Then the latency SLO thresholds are 3500 ms (p95), 2000 ms (p50), 8000 ms and retrieval 300 and 700 ms.
Given docs/runbooks/slo.md, When reviewed, Then it states the two windows, burn rates 14.4 and 6, and the failing-request definition (checked by a presence test in scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py).
Given the drill in E9-T17 injects a 20% error rate for 10 min in a scratch prod-profile project, Then the fast burn alert opens.

tickets.title: Terraform: chat and retrieval alert policies
tickets.summary: Alert policies exist for degraded turns, rerank 429, LLM fallback, readiness failing and model retirement.
tickets.description:
Implements these alerts from overview.md 9.5: "degraded turns > 5% in 15 min, rerank 429 > 0, LLM fallback in use, readiness failing, model retirement soon".
Add terraform/alerts_chat.tf with google_monitoring_alert_policy resources using the E9-T11 notification channel:
- degraded_turns: retrieval_degraded_ratio > 0.05 over a 15 min window.
- rerank_429: rate of rerank_429_total > 0 over 5 min.
- llm_fallback_in_use: llm_fallback_total increase > 0 over 5 min.
- readiness_failing: readiness_failing = 1 for 3 min (metric from E9-T8).
- model_retirement_soon: model_retirement_days (gauge, R74) < 30 for 5 min; the alert is on the gauge, not a log line.
Thresholds are tfvars with these defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Given terraform plan, When listed, Then five policies exist with the names above (terraform show -json assertion in scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py).
Given the degraded_turns policy JSON, Then threshold 0.05 and duration 900 s.
Given the E9-T17 drill emits rerank_429_total=1, When 5 minutes pass, Then the rerank_429 incident opens (drill record in docs/runbooks/alert-drills.md).

tickets.title: Alert drill runbook and script
tickets.summary: A script and runbook fire each 9.5 alert in a scratch project and record the result, covering the Done-when drill.
tickets.description:
Implements the Done-when item: "Each alert in overview.md#9.5 fires in a drill (degraded turns > 5% in 15 min, rerank 429, outbox age, ACL applier lag, DEFAULT partition non-empty, readiness failure, budget)". Add scripts/alert_drill.py and docs/runbooks/alert-drills.md. The script takes an alert name, injects the condition (writes the matching log-metric line or metric value for the alert; real fault injection where cheap: stop acl-applier, insert a DEFAULT partition row, flip a role flag for readiness, lower budget), polls the Cloud Monitoring API until an incident opens or a timeout (default 15 min), then clears the condition and reports PASS or FAIL as JSON. Include the burn-rate, LLM fallback, consumer lag, DLQ and model-retirement alerts too. The runbook records the date, result and incident link per alert, and a manual check that the E9-T10 trace appears in Cloud Trace.
Runs only against the scratch project named by a required --project argument and refuses ENV_PROFILE=prod project ids listed in a deny var.
The drill also covers the llm_cost_usd_total budget alert and the model_retirement_days alert; the DEFAULT-partition drill waits up to 45 min.
acceptance_criteria: Given a scratch project with E9-T11 to E9-T16 applied, When python scripts/alert_drill.py --all runs, Then each alert in overview.md 9.5 returns PASS in the JSON and the process exits 0; exit non-zero if any fails.
Given a project where one policy is removed, When the script runs, Then that alert reports FAIL (negative control).
Given --project equals a name in the deny list, Then the script exits 2 without calling any API (unit test).
Given docs/runbooks/alert-drills.md, Then it has a row per alert in 9.5 (presence test in scripts/check_monitoring_tf.py).
